### Summary

If you start the game in Russian and play a game that includes a Russian PO file in any mod, Luanti reports the following error message:

> Invalid Plural-Forms line: [...]

(abridged, the "[...]" represents the Plural-Forms line it complains about)

This error message is from `translation.cpp`.

The Plural-Forms line in question is:

```
"Plural-Forms: nplurals=3; plural=n%10==1 && n%100!=11 ? 0 : n%10>=2 && "
"n%10<=4 && (n%100<10 || n%100>=20) ? 1 : 2;\n"
```

Yes, these are 2 lines but changing it to:

```
"Plural-Forms: nplurals=3; plural=n%10==1 && n%100!=11 ? 0 : n%10>=2 && n%10<=4 && (n%100<10 || n%100>=20) ? 1 : 2;\n"
```

does not fix it either. I am pretty certain this is valid syntax because basically the same line is used for the Luanti engine PO file for Russian, the only difference is that the `plurals` expression is enclosed in 2 additional brackets. Adding those to my game did not make the error go away either but really it shouldn't make a difference.
This expression looks valid to me, it's also literally in the gettext manual. According to the gettext manual (<https://www.gnu.org/software/gettext/manual/html_node/Plural-forms.html>), the `plurals` expression is C code with some restrictions. And to be extra sure, I wrote a tiny C program with this expression to see if it compiles. It compiles.

I therefore suspect there is an error in Luanti's expression parser.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a game or mod with a Russian PO file. Use the aforementioned Plural-Forms line. Alternatively, use Repixture 3.17.2
2. Set language to Russian
3. Restart Luanti
4. Start the game or mod

* Expected: No error message
* Actual result: Error messages
